solution: Squaring and adding: \((3\sin P + 4\cos Q)^2 + (4\sin Q + 3\cos P)^2 = 36 + 1 = 37\). Expanding: \(9 + 16 + 24(\sin P\cos Q + \cos P\sin Q) = 25 + 24\sin(P+Q) = 37\), so \(\sin(P+Q) = \frac{1}{2}\). Thus \(P + Q = \frac{\pi}{6}\) or \(\frac{5\pi}{6}\). If \(P + Q = \frac{\pi}{6}\), then \(P < \frac{\pi}{6}\), so \(3\sin P < \frac{3}{2}\) and \(3\sin P + 4\cos Q < \frac{3}{2} + 4 < 6\), which is impossible. So \(P + Q = \frac{5\pi}{6}\) and \(R = \pi - \frac{5\pi}{6} = \frac{\pi}{6}\). Hence (A).
